cases.claim: All 384 document jobs in the accepted native experiment returned correct results.
evidence_a: A1: Accepted native run completed 384/384 document tasks correctly.
evidence_b: B1: Correctness was checked against deterministic expected document answers. This claim concerns that accepted run only.

cases.claim: The accepted experiment proves IPvX is ready for the global public Internet.
evidence_a: A2: The real experiment used 16 processes and completed all 384 tasks.
evidence_b: B2: All 16 processes ran on a single VM in isolated namespaces. Admission was fixed. No WAN, independent operators, hostile peers or large routing table was tested.

cases.claim: Duplicate delivery caused extra application executions in the accepted run.
evidence_a: A3: The accepted run deliberately replayed 23 identical requests and logged 80 retries.
evidence_b: B3: Durable receipt checks counted exactly 384 unique executions for the 384 original tasks. Replayed requests returned the saved receipt.

cases.claim: Existing measurements show native IPvX is faster than ordinary IP for language-model agents.
evidence_a: A4: Accepted document-task latency p50 was 459 ms, p95 was 1321 ms.
evidence_b: B4: That experiment contained no language models and no ordinary-IP baseline. It cannot establish a comparative speed result.

scope: Only task claims and supplied evidence; private logs and network identifiers excluded.
